newsitem.title: USA: Third shuttle Challenger piece recovered in Fla..
newsitem.headline: Third shuttle Challenger piece recovered in Fla..

text.p: The Atlantic Ocean gave up another piece of the space shuttle Challenger on Wednesday, one day after two large sections of the ill-fated spacecraft washed up on Florida's coast.
"Another piece washed up on shore at Cocoa Beach this morning and some citizens found it and took it to the police department," Bruce Buckingham, a NASA spokesman at the Kennedy Space Centre, said.
He said NASA sent a team to retrieve what was identified as another section of Challenger's left wing. "It has been identified as a smaller piece off the larger piece we found yesterday."

The piece found on Wednesday was a 10-inch (25-cm) by 15-inch (37.5-cm) section of the flap of Challenger's left wing. Like two larger pieces of the wing found on Cocoa Beach on Tuesday, the first big pieces of the spacecraft found in years, it was encrusted with barnacles after spending nearly 11 years underwater.

An explosion ripped Challenger apart 73 seconds after blastoff on Jan. 28, 1986, killing all seven people on board, six astronauts and New Hampshire teacher Christa McAuliffe, selected through a Teacher in Space programme. The astronauts who died were Francis Scobee, Michael Smith, Judith Resnik, Ronald McNair, Ellison Onizuka and Gregory Jarvis.

A massive recovery operation was mounted after the disaster but only about half of the orbiter was ever retrieved. NASA said the debris found this week was the first section of the left wing to be recovered but it did not expect to learn anything new about the cause of the tragedy, the result of a solid rocket booster joint failure.

Cocoa Beach residents said bits of the debris had been taken by souvenir hunters on Tuesday before police arrived, an action that would be subject to prosecution. But NASA said it had had no confirmation.
"If we hear of anybody that has a piece, then we certainly will ask them to return it, because it is government property," Buckingham said.
